Admissions by unapproved medical/
dental colleges
*181. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have not renewed/given permission to some
medical/dental colleges as they are lagging
behind in infrastructure;
(b) whether it is also a fact that such
colleges are still admitting the students; and
(c) the steps being taken by Government
to save the future of aspiring students?
Development of towns in Andhra
Pradesh
*182. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the number of medium and small
towns having population upto five lakhs in
Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the details of amount sanctioned and
expenditure incurred by Government during
the last five years for their development,
year-wise; and
(c) the results achieved during the said
period?
Work culture of CPWD
*183. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned "A
case of shocking apathy", which appeared
in the Hindu, (Delhi), dated the
30th September, 2001;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) the action taken against the guilty
officers of CPWD; and
(d) the fresh steps taken/proposed to be
taken by Government to improve the work
culture of CPWD?
Hearing by Special Courts for
undertrial prisoners
*184. DR. A.K. PATEL: Will the
Minister of LAW, JUSTICE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of undertrial prisoners

for whom hearing has been held till October,
2001, after the orders for setting up of special
courts in jails passed by the Honourable
Supreme Court;
(b) the details thereof, State-wise; and
(c) whether Government propose to put
more efforts in this direction?
Cases pending in various High Courts
and Supreme Court
*185. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN:
PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
 Will the Minister of LAW, JUSTICE
AND COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that huge arrears of
cases are pending in various High Courts and
the Supreme  Court as these cases drag on
for years due to unscrupulous laws, floppy
and inadequate police investigations;
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith the
number of cases pending in these courts, the
time since pending and the reasons for
pendency; and
(c) the details of steps taken or proposed
to be taken by Government to clear the backlog
of the cases in the interest of
litigants?
Monitoring of AIDS/HIV
*186. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH:
SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) how Government monitor the
functioning of NGOs working on AIDS/HIV;
and
(b) the steps taken to curb the menace of
AIDS spreading at alarming speed in Andhra
Pradesh and Maharashtra?
Basic Minimum Service Programme
in Gujarat
*187. SHRI BRAHMAKUMAR
BHATT: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of basic services
provided under Basic Minimum Service
Programme;
(b) the number of villages in Gujarat
where Primary Health Centres have not
been opened, so far;
(c) the funds allocated as Additional
Central Assistance to Gujarat for the last
three years for Basic Minimum Service
Programme;
(d) the amount earmarked by State
Government and Central assistance for
PHCs in Gujarat for the last two years;
and
(e) the amount utilised on PHCs?
Tribal belts in Gujarat
*188. SHRI AHMED PATEL: Will
the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that tribals form
15 per cent of the total population of
Gujarat;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
tribal belts identified in the State, district-
wise;
(c) the programmes and schemes being
implemented for the development of tribals
in the State; and
(d) the funds allocated to the State
during the last five years, year-wise and
programme-wise?
